Here is a simple example of a Pygame game that displays FPS counter in the top left corner and quits the game when the 'ESC' key is pressed:

import pygame
import time
import sys

pygame.init()

# Set up the display
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((640, 480))
pygame.display.set_caption("Simple Pygame Game")

# Set up the clock
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Set up the font
font = pygame.font.Font(None, 36)

# Set up the FPS counter
fps = 0
fps_text = font.render("FPS: 0", True, (0, 255, 0))

# Game loop
running = True
while running:
    # Event handling
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                running = False

    # Clear the screen
    screen.fill((0, 0, 0))

    # Draw the FPS counter
    fps_text = font.render("FPS: " + str(int(clock.get_fps())), True, (0, 255, 0))
    screen.blit(fps_text, (10, 10))

    # Update the display
    pygame.display.flip()

    # Cap the framerate
    clock.tick(60)

# Quit Pygame
pygame.quit()
sys.exit()

import pygame
import time
import sys

pygame.init()

# Set up the display
WIDTH, HEIGHT = 800, 600
display = pygame.display.set_mode((WIDTH, HEIGHT))
pygame.display.set_caption("PyGame Project")

# Set up the clock
clock = pygame.time.Clock()

# Set up the FPS counter
font = pygame.font.Font(None, 36)
fps_text = font.render("FPS: 0", True, (255, 255, 255))

# Game loop
running = True
while running:
    # Event handling
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            running = False
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
                running = False

    # Update the FPS counter
    now = pygame.time.get_ticks()
    dt = now - prev_time
    fps = int(1000 / dt)
    fps_text = font.render("FPS: %d" % fps, True, (255, 255, 255))
    prev_time = now

    # Fill the display
    display.fill((0, 0, 0))

    # Draw the FPS counter
    display.blit(fps_text, (0, 0))

    # Update the display
    pygame.display.flip()

    # Cap the FPS
    clock.tick(60)

# Quit PyGame
pygame.quit()
sys.exit()
